_comment: Binaries and payloads actually embedded in the shipped app bundle (not installed on demand). Read by scripts/release/generate-notices.py to build THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES. URLs must be pinned: {pin:<identity>} expands to that dependency's Package.resolved commit, and generation fails on any branch-following GitHub URL. Keep in sync with what Contents/Resources actually contains.

bootstrapBinaries.notes: Bundled bootstrap binary used to create and manage per-tool conda environments under ~/.lungfish. Version and sha256 are sourced from third-party-tools-lock.json bootstrap.micromamba.

managedToolNotes.note: LGE uses a separately maintained custom fork of upstream PrimalScheme3 v3.3.0, not an upstream release (https://github.com/dhoconno/primalscheme3-lge). The exact custom version, release artifact checksum, and fork/upstream revisions are pinned in third-party-tools-lock.json (packTools[primalscheme3].pythonRuntime). The fork adds a selectable terminal-missing-data policy; its Python observed-only discovery path differs from the upstream Rust legacy path. Upstream source: https://github.com/artic-network/primalscheme3, licensed GPL-3.0. Upstream authors retain their copyrights; modified source, attribution and the complete license are available in the public fork. This tool is installed into a separate managed environment on demand and is not included in the app executable. LGE's MIT license does not replace this tool's GPL license.

Olivar 1.3.3 is installed on demand into its own managed environment from a checksum-bound osx-arm64 explicit conda lock. Source: https://github.com/treangenlab/Olivar, licensed GPL-3.0-or-later. It is not included in the app executable; LGE's MIT license does not replace the tool's GPL license.

varVAMP 1.3.2 is installed on demand into its own managed environment from a checksum-bound osx-arm64 explicit conda lock. Source: https://github.com/jonas-fuchs/varVAMP, licensed GPL-3.0-or-later. It is not included in the app executable; LGE's MIT license does not replace the tool's GPL license.

The Ribosomal RNA Removal Data (deacon-ribokmers) is the deacon minimizer index ribokmers.k31w15.idx (SHA-256 f88286f607bc062ef872b55cac9aff1d447f7106068cafefef72a3ba8e49ede6), which LGE hosts at https://dholk.primate.wisc.edu/_webdav/dho/public/lge/%40files/databases/deacon-ribokmers/k31w15-deacon0.16.0-1thread-2026-10-22/ and every install downloads on demand. It is not included in the app executable. It was built on one thread with deacon 0.16.0 (MIT, https://github.com/bede/deacon) from ribokmers.fa.gz (https://bbmap.org/resources/ribokmers.fa.gz, SHA-256 38607351140350d33c868919eb01aaa438c9b729470a094ab2eed55f8056fbf1), which Brian Bushnell made with BBTools and bbmap.org distributes. BBTools Copyright (c) 2014, The Regents of the University of California, through Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (subject to receipt of any required approvals from the U.S. Dept. of Energy). All rights reserved. BBTools is licensed BSD-3-Clause-LBNL, and its complete notice is in the NOTICE.txt beside the hosted file. The reference sequences derive from the SILVA SSU and LSU ribosomal RNA databases. SILVA is credited as the original author of that data, which SILVA licenses under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) as of release 138. BBTools does not name the SILVA release it used. The index changes the data's form from reference sequences to minimizers.

containerizationPayloads.notes: ARM64 Linux kernel boot image (Ubuntu 22.04 toolchain) used as the VM kernel for the Apple Containerization runtime that executes Nextflow/TaxTriage pipelines in an isolated Linux VM. Built from the upstream apple/containerization kernel recipe. GPL-2.0 requires this notice and a source offer; see sourceOffer.
